content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.3+ sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., -0.5 to 0.0) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, forecast remains high for 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights recent lows — correct by smoothing out extreme values in forecast tail.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early part of the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — reduce forecast slope in early days.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.3, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days; if sentiment < -0.3, increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days to counteract bias.
